cases.policy: Bare-hand feeding is a keeper-only duty at the otter pool.
Deputy librarians, and only deputy librarians, may admit readers after hours.
The say on campsite layout belongs to the site steward.
Signing off the muster sheet is a matter for the trek leader.
Photocopying the exhibit licence and the franking stamp is not authorised.
The route card and the telematics dump may not be copied.
No cream may be whipped without the pasteurisation log being initialled.
No seed potatoes leave the store without the inspector's chalk mark.
The new bandstand may not be booked until the safety certificate is framed at the lodge.
Sponsorship slides may not run on the scoreboard until the league has signed the media deal.
No more than four bales per lift on the goods hoist.
The hoist may be used provided the outriggers are pinned and the pad feet are on firm ground.
If the weir gauge reads amber or the by-wash is blocked, the canoe session is called off.
Loudspeakers are banned in the bird garden, except when the warden runs a dawn walk.
The society ledger stays sealed except for cases where the auditor general demands inspection.
When the bakehouse is running, apprentices may operate the divider, unless the miller is adjusting the stones.
Each speaker may collect only their own name badge.
A current tetanus booster is sufficient for entry to the muck yard.
Completing the chain-saw course is necessary before any felling work.
All visitors are obliged to dip their boots at the gate.
Only fitters who have logged the morning calibration may true the lathe chucks.
Wardens on the night roster may issue spare hut keys to walkers in distress.
Duty skippers may call the ice breaker when the channel gauge shows plate ice.
After the gales have passed, the boardwalk may reopen, except where the deck planks are still sprung.
Once the curd has set, the cutting frames may be lowered, unless the vat reads above thirty-two degrees.
Blasting may proceed only after the bird-scarer rounds finish, except when the shot-fireer calls a weather hold.
The melt index and the batch code are to be taken from the furnace terminal alone, each logged on its own line.
Weights for the rams and the ewes go on separate cards; the veterinary scale printout is the only acceptable source.
Recording the till serials is not optional whenever the floats cabinet is unlocked.
Unless the moisture meter dissents, the floorboards must acclimatize in the room for a fortnight.
When the anemometer is not showing red, kite flying is permitted at the seaward end.
At most six guests per members' screening, unless the director opens the circle seats.
No more than two dogs off the lead per handler, except at the retired-greyhound sessions.
Provided the loom is not mid-pick, the warp tension may be adjusted.
If the estate gate is not chained after midnight, the patrol must log it.
So long as the reservoir is not drawn down past the second ledge, anglers may fish the tower bank.
Once the fair ends, the show-jump wings and the plastic cups are to be stacked together on the trolley.
Before the sea mist rolls in, the waymarkers and the rope lines are to be checked, each on its own round.
Caddies may take the buggy onto the fringe, except when the greenskeeper has flagged the dew.
Trainee helpers may open the petting barn, save when the vet has sealed the lambing wing.
No food or drink may be taken into the map room.
Neither the junior rowers nor the novice coxes may launch the double scull.
The meadow may be mown only ahead of the orchid count.

Radio spares live in the locked drawer, and that drawer is the duty operator's domain. Nobody else takes so much as a fuse from it. The one exception is the treasurer, who may raid it on club nights for the raffle microphone.

The drying barn is a dust hazard while the malt turn is running, so power drills stay out of the bins for the whole turn. If a bin sensor needs fitting mid-turn, the maltster can authorize it, but only in writing.
Wardens who find a gate unlatched on the dawn round, and who cannot account for it in the movement book, must report it to the head office before their shift ends.
The annexe kitchen may be used by hirers once the caretaker has walked them through the shut-off valves (a five-minute routine, no appointment needed), and by nobody who has skipped that walkthrough.
It is open to any member who has held a full licence for two seasons to take the rescue boat out single-handed, weather card permitting.
Lamps fitted by the visiting engineer, and still bearing her lead tag, may not be swapped out by the volunteer crew.
When the ringing is over, the tower door and the rope cupboard are locked up together with the sexton's key.

The serving hatch opens at noon sharp for the lunch crowd. Hatch duty is the Saturday volunteers' alone, and they keep it even when the coordinator is away; the only time they stand down is a confirmed norovirus alert, when the paid staff take over.

The treatment room runs on a two-bin system. Clinical waste waits in the yellow lobby for the contractor's van, and nothing from that lobby - no gloves, no wrappers, nothing - ever goes into the general skip at the back gate.

Stock figures are a headache at the heritage railway shop, so here is the rule: the till roll totals and the float counts are copied across from the EPOS report, and that report is the only source the auditor accepts. Tote-board estimates and mental arithmetic do not count.
Two faults will stop the press: the web-break sensor tripping, or the folder jamming past three sheets. Either one, and the printer on shift must kill the drive before leaving the cage.
Strimming the cliff path is the warden's job alone (insurance, sadly), and only when the risk register shows the wind below force five.
For the flock counts, the pasture app is the sole source; counts from memory do not count.
Running the buffer and the polisher off one extension lead is not allowed.
Two standing rules for the lamp room: do not repaint the brass, and do not reorder the lenses.
The glue pot is never to be heated over an open flame.
Under no circumstances may the master key be lent to tenants.
Every batch ticket must be hole-punched at the weigh station.
Staff are required to hang their fobs on the pegboard at the end of each shift.
The staff-room toaster may be used at any time.
Members may bring one guest to the society supper.
If the tide board reads low water, the ford crossing may be attempted.
When the booking sheet shows a free piste, the practice track may be reserved.
Frost blankets may be deployed only while the irrigation is shut down.
Only with the duty coxswain's consent can the rescue launch leave its berth.
The annexe may be unlocked if and only if the museum is open to the public.
Access to the drop zone is granted exactly when the jump manifest is closed.
Smoking is forbidden on the viewing terrace, except during the licensed festival.
Parking on the access road is banned, except when the overflow field is sodden.
Only the duty sound engineer may patch the mixing desk.
Resetting the breaker is reserved to the qualified electrician.
Provided that the sump lamp is lit, the bilge pump may be run.
The drying racks may be loaded once the extract fan has started.
It is mandatory to log every helium transfer in the cylinder book.
Cellulose thinners must never be stored beside the compressor.
Only once the dust extractor has reached speed may grinding begin.
After the drag pack has passed, the footpath may be reopened.
